msg: Hola, buen día. Somos un grupo de 7 amigas de Bogotá. Tres ya tenemos el Open Water, dos quieren probar el minicurso y dos prefieren snorkel. ¿Cuánto saldría por persona saliendo desde Cartagena y hay descuento por grupo?
reply:
¡Hola! 🪸 Soy *Coral*, de *Diving Planet* — buceamos todo el año en las Islas del Rosario, saliendo desde Cartagena o desde las propias islas. 🌊

¡Buen día! ¡Qué chévere plan para las siete! Sí, pueden combinar buceo certificado, minicurso y snorkel en la misma salida; según la operación, podrían ir en la misma lancha o dividirse por actividad.

Te dejo a continuación los precios por persona saliendo desde Cartagena. Para un grupo de 7, aplica un 10% de descuento de grupo en buceo recreativo, minicurso y snorkel; hay que solicitarlo antes de pagar. Se suma al descuento online y no aplica a cursos PADI.

Como son de Bogotá, ¿todas tienen nacionalidad colombiana o residencia en Colombia? La moneda depende de eso; si el grupo incluye personas extranjeras sin residencia colombiana, toda la reserva se paga en USD.

*Precios por persona* (online · normal):
• Minicurso de Buceo: 655.000 COP · 727.000 COP
• Tour de Snorkeling: 448.000 COP · 497.000 COP
• Salidas de Buceo - 2 inmersiones (1 día): 630.000 COP · 700.000 COP
• Paquete de 3 inmersiones (1 día, 2 diurnas + 1 nocturna): 1.017.000 COP · 1.130.000 COP
• Paquete de 4 inmersiones (2 días, 4 diurnas): 1.154.000 COP · 1.282.000 COP

No hay descuento ni tarifa especial por ser colombiano: el precio es el mismo, solo cambia la moneda (COP).

Te recomiendo el plan de *2 inmersiones en 1 día* en las Islas del Rosario. (Si prefieres más inmersiones, hay *paquetes* de 3 o más; dímelo.)

¿Ha pasado *más de 2 años* desde la última inmersión de alguno del grupo?

msg: Hello. My wife and I arrive on a cruise ship in Cartagena on March 3rd, docking at 7:00 am and we must be back on board by 5:00 pm. We would both like to snorkel. Is that doable? We are from Canada.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Snorkeling in the Rosario Islands is a wonderful day out, but the Cartagena tour won’t fit your cruise schedule: it departs at 8:00 a.m. from Muelle de la Bodeguita and returns to Cartagena around 4:15 p.m., leaving too little time to get back on board by 5:00 p.m. The departure time can’t be moved earlier.

So, would you leave *from Cartagena* (Muelle de la Bodeguita)? 🚤

Diving Planet policies:
- Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). The refresher is also 18 hours: it is for certified divers, even though it is booked as the mini course. The hours count from the last dive, not from the return to Cartagena. The mini course dive ends around 12:00 (noon): its 12 hours count from then. If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.
- If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.
- For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
- Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center, at 8:00 AM. Departing from Cartagena there is no hotel pick-up: each person gets to the dock on their own (ground transportation to the dock is not included).
- By booking you accept our terms and conditions, cancellation policy, and data treatment. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Date changes are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Changes to the number of people on a booking you already made are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Colombians (anyone with Colombian nationality, holding a Colombian cédula or passport, wherever they live; also dual nationals when one nationality is Colombian) and residents of Colombia (holders of a cédula de extranjería, a resident ID; living in Colombia without one is not enough) pay in Colombian pesos (COP). Saying they are Colombian or from a Colombian city ("I'm from Cali") already says it; what is not enough is only having been born there while living abroad: then ask whether they hold Colombian nationality or a cédula de extranjería. All other international clients pay in US dollars (USD). A group does not pay in parts: if the same booking mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group pays in US dollars (USD), residents and Colombians included. A Colombian together with someone who holds a cédula de extranjería, wherever they are from, is not a mixed group: both pay in pesos (COP). The price is the same: only the currency changes (there is no discount for being Colombian).
- If the group mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group booking is paid in US dollars (USD), at the same equivalent price. Someone with a cédula de extranjería does not count as a foreigner, wherever they are from. There is no different price for being Colombian.
- If you are already on the Rosario Islands, we coordinate pick-up and drop-off from hotels with maritime access. In some cases the boat arrives directly at the hotel; in others we indicate the nearest dock or meeting point.
- These plans have different prices because they do not include transport from Cartagena or lunch.
- Pick-up is only on the Rosario Islands: Barú (including Playa Blanca, which is on Barú) is not part of the islands and we do not operate or pick up there; guests staying in Barú depart from Cartagena (Muelle de la Bodeguita).
- It depends on the activity: snorkeling from 6 years old; Bubble Makers from 8 to 10 years old (pool mini-course and very shallow water practice, max 2 meters); the dive mini-course and the Open Water course from 10 years old; the Advanced course and the Rescue course from 12. Minors must be accompanied by a demonstrable parent or responsible relative.
- The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). The link can be sent together with the booking link; if you have not completed it, it is sent again in the booking confirmation email. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.
- If you are a certified diver, there are no additional medical restrictions; your liability waiver is the certified-diver one: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). For the refresher day this one is not used: use the course medical form.
- Bringing or drinking alcohol on the boat or during the activity is not allowed, and no alcohol or other substances may be consumed before diving. You must be in good physical condition.
- The booking system on our website. It automatically closes at 4:30 PM the day before: after that time you can no longer book for the next day, and you still book on the website for the next available day.
- To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.
- From Cartagena: departure at 8:00 a.m. from Muelle de la Bodeguita and return at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.). From the islands: hotel pick-up between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (8:00 a.m. for specialties and 7:30 a.m. on day 2 of some courses). Daytime activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m. (see the activity schedule). Night diving: in the evening (pick-up around 5:30 p.m., back around 7:30 p.m.). Online booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before; after that, you book on the website for the next available day.
- We only close on December 25 and January 1. The rest of the year we operate every day, including public holidays, except for suspension due to adverse weather conditions.
- The tour includes water all day, coconut candy between dives, and lunch (rice with chicken or rice with vegetables). The menu is always the same, it does not change by day/supplier. Vegetarians, vegans, and celiacs receive rice with vegetables. Guests may bring their own food if needed (e.g. allergy or special diet). If the guest has a food allergy, they must inform us before the tour. In multi-day packages departing from Cartagena, lunch is included on the first day only; plans for guests already on the islands do not include lunch.
- Photos and videos are not offered proactively or included in the price. The instructor may take them voluntarily and delivers them by the next day at the latest. Any tip to the instructor for photos/videos is voluntary: each guest gives whatever they like, directly to them. This applies to every activity, including the mini-course (and the refresher, booked as a mini-course), PADI courses and certified-diver trips: not included, the instructor may take them voluntarily.
- The 3, 4, 5, 7 and 9 dive packages are exclusively for certified divers with a minimum Open Water level. They are not available for uncertified beginners.
- Two-day courses (Open Water, Referral Course, Advanced, Rescue and Mindful Diving) require accommodation on the islands: at least one night, the night of day 1 (there is no return to Cartagena on day 1). There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel. The same goes for multi-day dive packages (4, 5, 7 and 9 dives): you stay on the islands, and accommodation, which is not included, is booked directly with the hotel.
- Private services and closed groups are available, with no fixed price (it depends on the group and the date). A member of our team prepares the quote and coordinates an available instructor for the date.
- Through DIVE TO HEAL, more than 360 people with disabilities have been served. Accepted conditions include: hearing impairment (deaf), visual impairment (blind), reduced mobility (wheelchair), Down Syndrome, Cerebral Palsy, and Autism (depending on level and assessment). All instructors are trained in adaptive diving. Advance notice is recommended. The limitation is the presence of additional medical conditions that contraindicate diving.
- If you're already on the Rosario Islands and your hotel has maritime access, boat pick-up and drop-off are included at no extra charge.
- We dive in the Rosario Islands, inside the Corales del Rosario y San Bernardo National Natural Park, about 45-60 minutes by boat from Cartagena.
- All daytime activities (dive trips, mini-course, snorkeling, courses and each day of the packages) end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., followed by lunch. Guests departing from Cartagena have lunch included on the islands and the boat returns to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.); guests staying on the islands return to their hotel around 12:00-1:00 p.m. for lunch (lunch not included). On overnight courses and packages, day 1's daytime activities also end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., and then you go to your hotel on the islands. Night diving (on plans that include it) is separate, in the evening (see each plan's schedule).
- There is always availability (confirmed by the business). We only close on December 25 and January 1, and a trip can be suspended due to adverse weather. The date and number of people are chosen in the booking link. To book for the next day, you need to do it before 4:30 p.m. (see booking system cutoff). Booking for the SAME day is no longer possible (trips leave in the morning and the website closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before): you book for the next available day.
- Each person can bring one backpack or bag on the boat. If the guest needs to bring a suitcase, it has to be arranged with a member of our team. If they prefer not to take it, we can store the suitcase at our office in Cartagena.
- What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.
- At our base on the island there are lockers where you can leave your things (clothes, phone, wallet) while you dive or snorkel.
- There is no minimum number of people: every activity runs even for a single person.
- Activities and courses are taught in Spanish and English. If a participant speaks neither language, they can come with someone who interprets for them, but instruction is still given in Spanish or English.
- Bookings are made on our website, through each activity's link (with the 10% online discount). The system closes at 4:30 PM the day before: after that time you still book on the website, for the next available day. Plans with no booking link (the 3- and 4-dive packages, the 9-dive package from the islands, the 1-dive trip from the islands, Bubble Makers, Divemaster and the private service) are booked by an advisor in this chat.
- Besides the insurance form, each diver fills in a liability waiver. Our team sends it to you to complete (certified divers: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish)), and the confirmation email reminds you if you have not done it yet.
- The mini-course is a one-day try-dive, an introduction to diving: it does not certify, does not count as part of any PADI course and requires nothing from PADI beforehand (no PADI account or PADI online course). It is the same departing from Cartagena or already on the islands: there is no online or emailed theory; the theory is done there, on the day, along with pool practice and 1 ocean dive with an instructor.
- International clients pay 100% by card on the website; with a foreign card the passport is used as the ID document.
- Colombians and residents of Colombia (including holders of a cédula de extranjería) pay in pesos and do not use the website booking link: a team advisor always closes the booking in this chat and sends them the link, QR code or Llave to pay 100% online or a 50% deposit, and the other 50% on the day of the activity, by card or cash. The 50% deposit option is only for them. Nobody pays 100% at the dock without booking online.
- If you leave the next day around noon: from the Rosario Islands it is very tight (pickup is between 9:30 and 9:45 and the activity ends around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), so it is best to confirm it with a team advisor; departing from Cartagena it does not fit (the boat returns at 3:00 p.m. and arrives around 4:15 p.m.). To book for the next day you must do it before 4:30 p.m. the day before.
- Customers paying in US dollars book and pay through the online link: the payment is recorded right away and the team reconciles it shortly after to confirm the booking; only if the online payment fails does the team send a link to pay by transfer.
- If the booking system or the online payment fails, our team sends you a link to pay by bank transfer, and the 10% online discount is kept (because the online payment failed). Outside that case there is no payment by transfer: the 10% discount is for booking and paying online.
- In groups combining diving and snorkeling, snorkeling takes place in a different area from the dive sites. If there are few people everyone goes on the same boat; otherwise the group is split by activity.
- Besides our base (Hotel San Pedro de Majagua and Hotel Cocoliso, on Isla Grande), other hotels in the area with maritime access are Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras and Pao Pao. Accommodation is not included: it is booked directly with the hotel.
- To book an activity departing from the islands, the customer must already have their hotel and tell us which one: pickup is arranged there. If they don't have it yet, they first book the hotel and message us with its name; then we book. If they booked the activity first, the hotel could be cancelled, it could be full, they could forget to tell us or end up departing from Cartagena. If they stay in a house, an Airbnb or a hotel not on our list, they tell us the name and an advisor confirms the pickup before they book and pay: they do not book until then.
- Returning to Cartagena on a different date from the plan is not included. If the guest wants to stay longer on the islands and come back with us another day, a member of our team arranges it (space on the boat, etc.).
- Departure and pickup times are fixed: they cannot be moved earlier or later. If you need an adjustment, a team advisor reviews it.
- Cancellations due to bad weather are unlikely because the Rosario Islands are in sheltered waters. If the Port Authority (Capitanía de Puerto) closes departures to the islands, we first try to reschedule the activity so you don't lose your booking. If rescheduling is not possible, you get a 100% refund. See the terms and conditions: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Scuba diving is not possible during pregnancy: no mini-course, no dive trips and no courses (DAN and obstetricians advise against it for the whole pregnancy). Surface snorkeling is possible, with her doctor's approval. Whoever comes with her can dive as usual.
- If you get seasick on the boat (the ride to the islands is about 1 hour by speedboat): have a light breakfast before leaving and consider seasickness tablets. If you take any medication, ask your doctor whether you can dive with it.
- We do issue invoices (also to companies). An advisor from our team coordinates the invoice details with the customer.
- There is no maximum age for diving: an older person can dive with the same medical form as everyone else.
- We carry oxygen and a first-aid kit on board, with trained staff, and there is an emergency protocol.
- Groups are small and follow PADI safety standards for each activity.
- The boat is a regular speedboat with no bathroom. On the islands we use the facilities of the hotel where lunch is served: that is where you change, use the bathroom and shower.
- Diving Planet has no parking of its own; there are public car parks in the old town area, and the easiest way to reach the pier is by taxi.
- There is no gift card, but you can book in someone else's name; the date and details are arranged with an advisor.
- Smoking is not allowed on the boat.
- Pets are not allowed on the boat: we go to a National Natural Park.
- Babies and young children who are not yet old enough for any activity (snorkeling starts at 6) can ride the boat with their parents at any age, and they ride free.
- You can bring your own camera on the dives or snorkeling, at your own risk. Diving Planet does not rent cameras.

msg: Hi, we're two Dutch divers, both Rescue Divers, in Cartagena from the 10th to the 16th. We bring our own full gear. We want to dive on three separate days from Cartagena, coming back to the city each night. What's the best price for us?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

That sounds like a great plan! From Cartagena, the regular Fun Dives trip is two dives in one day, with a same-day return to the city. For three separate days, you’d book that trip on each day.

The 5% own-equipment discount applies because you’re bringing complete gear, and it can be combined with the online discount. I’m leaving the per-person prices below; the exact total for your booking will be shown at checkout.

msg: Solo yo. ¿A qué hora me recogerían en el Cocoliso y tengo que llevar algo? Gracias.
reply:
En Cocoliso, la recogida es entre las 9:30 y las 9:45. Ten listo tu carné de buceo y lleva bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda; el equipo de buceo está incluido. Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresher. Después de bucear, espera al menos 18 horas antes de tomar un vuelo.

También necesitas:
• Estar listo a las 9:30 en tu hotel
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.

¿Han pasado *más de 2 años* desde tu última inmersión?

Diving activities start at age 8.

Minors must be accompanied by a responsible adult. The online discount is applied when booking directly through our website.

• Snorkeling Tour: 126 USD · 140 USD
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

msg: That's better, thank you. So my wife and I would do the 2 dives, our son the mini course and our daughter the snorkeling. If both of us are diving, who stays with our daughter while she's snorkeling, given she has to be accompanied? And do we all go on the same boat?
reply:
Great combo — that's a really nice way to have everyone in the water on the same day! 🌊

On the accompaniment: minors must be accompanied by a responsible adult, so the snorkeling group is where your daughter needs a parent with her. Since you and your wife are both diving, the practical way is for one of you to join her snorkeling while the other dives, and then swap for the second dive — the team on board can help you coordinate that on the day. Snorkeling also takes place in a different area from the dive sites.

About the boat: in groups that combine diving and snorkeling, if there are few people everyone goes on the same boat; if the group is larger, they split by activity. Either way, you're all out on the water together for the day.

And just to keep it clear: the mini-course is a 1-day introductory experience, not a certification, so it's a separate booking from the certified 2-dive trip — each one is booked on its own.

Has it been *more than 2 years* since any diver in the group last dived?

msg: Good afternoon. I am from Germany and I hold an Open Water certification, although I have not dived for three years. I am staying in Getsemaní and I would like to dive next Wednesday. My flight home leaves on Thursday at 22:00. Is this possible, and what would you recommend?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

You can fly from **7:00 a.m. on Thursday** after a daytime refresher, so your Thursday 22:00 flight meets the 18-hour interval. The wait is counted from your last dive, not from your return to Cartagena.

Since you’re certified and haven’t dived for three years, I’d recommend a **Refresher**. It’s booked as the Dive Mini Course, but certified divers must observe the full 18-hour wait. The daytime activity ends around 12:00–1:00 p.m.; the boat returns to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m., arriving around 4:15 p.m. You’ll meet at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m.

You can choose Wednesday in the booking calendar here: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=en. The website closes bookings for the next day at 4:30 p.m. the day before.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

There is always availability: we operate every day, including public holidays, except December 25 and January 1; if sea conditions are not safe, the trip is rescheduled.

Would you like to book the refresher?

After your last dive, wait at least 18 hours before flying; for a daytime dive, that means flying from 7:00 a.m. the next day.

msg: Good, thank you. Two last questions: do you pick me up in Getsemaní or how do I reach the dock, and do I have to bring my certification card or fill in any forms for these two days?
reply:
There’s no hotel pick-up in Getsemaní. Please make your own way to **Muelle de la Bodeguita** for the 8:00 a.m. departure; ground transport to the dock isn’t included. At the entrance, ask for **Diving Planet at Gate 3**. [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Muelle+de+la+Bodeguita/@10.4199447,-75.5537609,828m/data=!3m2!1e3!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x8ef62f753729822d:0x1bbcdd8224d0eaaf!8m2!3d10.4199447!4d-75.551186!16s%2Fg%2F113gzkckf?entry=ttu)

Please bring your **Open Water certification card**—you can also send a photo beforehand or show it on the day. For the refresher, complete the **course medical form**: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. You’ll also need the insurance form from your booking confirmation email. The certified-diver liability waiver is **not** used for the refresher. The forms are in Spanish, and the confirmation email will remind you if anything is still outstanding.

You'll also need:
• There is no theory to do beforehand: it is done there, on the day, with the instructor.
• If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.
• After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying
• Minimum age: 10 and over.
• For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
• What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.

msg: Hey! I'm an American diver, Advanced Open Water. I'm renting a house on Airbnb on Isla Grande next week, it's called Villa Marea. I'd like to do two dives. Can you pick me up there? How does that work?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Great that you're staying on Isla Grande — you're right in the heart of the Rosario Islands, and the diving there is beautiful. 🤿

About pick-up: since you're staying in a house/Airbnb (Villa Marea) and not at one of our base hotels, an advisor needs to confirm the pick-up logistics with you before you book and pay. If the house has maritime access, the boat can often come directly; if not, we'll point you to the nearest dock or meeting point. So the first step is for the team to check Villa Marea and confirm the exact pick-up point and time.

How the day works once you're picked up:
- Hotel pick-up between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (if the house has boat access)
- Transfer to our base and equipment setup
- 2 open-water dives + surface interval at the base
- Return around 12:00–1:00 p.m.

For two dives from the islands, the plan is **Fun Dives – 2 dives (1 day, already on the islands)**: 124 USD / 440.000 COP online (138 USD / 489.000 COP regular). It includes gear, and certification is required — your Advanced Open Water is perfect. Lunch is not included on the island version.

Would you like me to connect you with a team advisor to confirm the pick-up at Villa Marea? Once that's confirmed, you can go ahead and book.

About pick-up: since you're staying in a house/Airbnb (Villa Marea) and not at one of our base hotels, an advisor needs to confirm the pick-up logistics with you before you book and pay. If the house has maritime access, the boat can often come directly; if not, we'll point you to the nearest dock or meeting point. So the first step is for the team to check Villa Marea and confirm the exact pick-up point and time.

How the day works once you're picked up:
- Hotel pick-up between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (if the house has boat access)
- Transfer to our base and equipment setup
- 2 open-water dives + surface interval at the base
- Return around 12:00–1:00 p.m.

For two dives from the islands, the plan is **Fun Dives – 2 dives (1 day, already on the islands)**: 124 USD / 440.000 COP online (138 USD / 489.000 COP regular). It includes gear, and certification is required — your Advanced Open Water is perfect. Lunch is not included on the island version.

Would you like me to connect you with a team advisor to confirm the pick-up at Villa Marea? Once that's confirmed, you can go ahead and book.

msg: Gracias. Nos interesa el minicurso, para los dos. ¿A qué profundidad se baja? Y mi esposa pregunta si hace falta saber nadar muy bien, porque ella nada lo justo. Quisiéramos ir el sábado 14 de noviembre.
reply:
El minicurso baja hasta 12 metros; lo habitual es entre 5 y 12, según el punto de buceo. No hace falta experiencia previa, pero no tengo a la mano el requisito específico sobre saber nadar. Como tu esposa nada lo justo, es importante que lo confirme un asesor antes de reservar. ¿Quieres que te pase con un asesor del equipo?

También necesitas:
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 12 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

Ten en cuenta que el minicurso es una iniciación de un día y no certifica; para certificarte está el curso Open Water (2 días, con noche en las islas).

Sobre el vuelo del domingo por la noche, el asesor ya tiene tu caso y te escribe por aquí.

También necesitas:
• Con este plan debes alojarte al menos 1 noche en las Islas del Rosario (hotel no incluido)

• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

msg: Hey! Planning a bachelor party in Cartagena in February, there will be 6 of us from Texas. Three of the guys are certified and three have never dived. We want one day out on the water together. What's the deal price-wise for a group like ours? And can we pay with US credit cards? One of us would pay for everybody.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

That sounds like a great day out on the water in the Rosario Islands! For the three certified divers, the one-day Cartagena option is **Fun Dives — 2 dives**. The three who haven’t dived can choose a **Dive Mini Course**, snorkeling, or come along as companions.

I’m leaving the prices below. Your group qualifies for the **10% group discount**, which can be combined with the **10% online discount**. The group discount must be requested before paying, and it applies to recreational diving, mini-courses, snorkeling, and companions.

Yes, international guests can pay by US credit card on the website. One person can pay for the group; with a foreign card, use the payer’s passport as the ID document. The certified dives and mini-course are separate bookings:

- Certified dives: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/salidas-de-buceo/1?language=en

msg: Good call on asking: one of the certified guys, Mike, last dived about three years ago. The other two dived last summer. No beers, got it. So what does Mike need to do? And who do I talk to on your team to get the group discount before we pay?
reply:
Since Mike last dived about three years ago, he’ll normally need a refresher before joining the certified dives. It’s a pool session and one dive with an instructor, and it takes a separate day, so he can’t do the refresher and the dive trip on the same day. If he has already completed a refresher or PADI ReActivate at another center, that counts. He should bring his certification card.

To get the group discount, contact the Diving Planet team and request it **before paying**. It’s a 10% group discount for 5 or more people, combined with the 10% online discount; it applies to recreational diving and mini-courses. I can offer to connect you with a team advisor.

You'll also need:
• There is no theory to do beforehand: it is done there, on the day, with the instructor.
• The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). The link can be sent together with the booking link; if you have not completed it, it is sent again in the booking confirmation email. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.
• To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.
• After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying
• Minimum age: 10 and over.
• What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.
• After diving, wait at least 12 hours before flying

Keep in mind that the mini-course is a one-day introduction and does not certify you; to get certified there is the Open Water course (2 days, with a night on the islands).

The *refresher* is an instructor-led review before diving again: it is booked as the *Dive Mini Course* and costs *183 USD* per person who needs it. It uses the course medical form (even for certified divers; the link comes with the booking). Are you interested?

msg: Good afternoon. My name is Anna, I am from Germany. I will stay at the Hotel San Pedro de Majagua on Isla Grande from November 20 to 24. reply:
Hi, Anna! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Good afternoon, Anna! Diving from Isla Grande is a lovely way to explore the Rosario Islands’ reefs. El refresher cuesta *183 USD online* o *204 USD a tarifa normal*. Incluye entrenamiento en piscina y una inmersión en el mar con instructor, además del equipo, almuerzo y traslados en lancha.

El refresher ocupa su propio día: no se puede combinar con la salida normal de dos inmersiones el mismo día. Como estarás en Cartagena del 2 al 6 de diciembre, podrías organizarlo en un día y hacer la salida de dos inmersiones en otro. El asesor ya tiene tu caso y te escribe por aquí para revisar el visto bueno y ayudarte con la reserva.

msg: Hiya! I'm Priya, a British backpacker on a tight budget, currently in Santa Marta and heading to Cartagena next week. I've got three free days, November 17 to 19, and I've always wanted to get my diving certification. Is that doable in three days, and what's the cheapest way of doing it? I've got a hostel in Getsemaní booked already.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Hiya, Priya! Getting certified is a fantastic way to experience the Rosario Islands. Yes, the Open Water course can fit within your three free days: it takes two days, with online theory beforehand. You’ll need to stay overnight on the islands after day one, though, so your Getsemaní hostel won’t cover that night.

The course price is listed below. The online price is the cheapest option; the discount is applied automatically when booking online. The course includes gear and lunch on day one, but not accommodation or lunch on day two. From Cartagena, you meet at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. and return around 4:15 p.m. on day two.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• PADI Basic Course (Open Water): 693 USD · 770 USD

Would you like to book the Open Water course for November 17–18 or 18–19?

msg: Brilliant. How long does the online theory take, and when do I get access to it? I'd have about a week to do it. Also, I need somewhere cheap to sleep on the island for that one night: do you know a budget option? And would I save anything by going to the island the day before and starting from there?
reply:
The Open Water eLearning takes about **10–12 hours** and must be completed before the practical training. Access is provided through PADI eLearning; the course information says it’s online theory, but doesn’t specify exactly when access is issued. A week should give you time to complete it.

Accommodation isn’t included, and I don’t have budget rates for the island hotels. You can book directly with a hotel; options with maritime access include Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras and Pao Pao. Staying at one of our base hotels, San Pedro de Majagua or Cocoliso, includes direct pickup.

The island-based course excludes the Cartagena boat transfer, so it may cost less, but I don’t have a listed price for that version of the Open Water course. You’d still need to arrange accommodation for the night.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• PADI Basic Course (Open Water): 693 USD · 770 USD

How many people would this be for: just you, or more? 😊

msg: Just me. Okay, I'll start from Cartagena then. What should I bring with me for the two days? I only have my big backpack, can I take it on the boat or leave it somewhere? I'd also love to bring my GoPro. And can I pay in cash when I arrive? My UK card charges me a fee abroad.
reply:
For the two days, bring your swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving gear is included. You can bring one backpack or bag on the boat, so your large backpack is fine. There are lockers at our island base for your belongings while you dive.

You’re welcome to bring your GoPro, though I don’t have specific information about camera rules or handling during the dives.

As an international guest, payment is 100% by card through the website when booking; cash payment on arrival isn’t available. The online booking includes a 10% discount.

🤿 *PADI Basic Course (Open Water)*
💰 *693 USD* per person (online rate)
📚 PADI course: dates, sessions and details are arranged with you.

👉 *For more information and to book, click here:*
https://book.divingplanet.org/book/basic-course/4?language=en

Guests who are not Colombian or residents of Colombia pay in US dollars (USD) by card on the website; the rate is the same, only the currency changes.

Is there anything else I can help you with? I can *add another activity*, answer questions, or adjust your booking. 🤿

msg: Okay, thanks. So who can tell me about the GoPro? I'd really like to film my first dives, it's kind of the whole point for me. And is storing my backpack at your office free? Last thing: I've got a flight to Medellín on the 19th at 9 in the morning, is that fine if I finish the course on the 18th?
reply:
You can bring your GoPro on the dives at your own risk. We don’t rent cameras, and underwater photos or videos aren’t included. An instructor may take photos or videos voluntarily, but that isn’t guaranteed—so I wouldn’t rely on that for filming your first dives.

You can bring one backpack on the boat. If you’d rather leave it at our Cartagena office, I don’t have the storage fee details handy.

For your 9:00 a.m. flight on the 19th: after the Open Water course, you must wait at least **18 hours from your last dive** before flying. The course’s second day returns to Cartagena around 4:15 p.m., but the return time doesn’t change the waiting period. I can’t confirm that the course schedule will leave enough time before your flight, so please check this timing with a team advisor before booking. Would you like me to connect you?

If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.

If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. msg: Our flight home leaves at 7:00 AM the day after we dive. Is that okay?
reply:
For certified divers, you need to wait at least **18 hours** after your last dive before flying, counting from the last dive itself (not from the return to Cartagena).

If your last dive is a daytime one (activities end around 12:00–1:00 p.m.), you can fly from **7:00 a.m. the next day** — so a 7:00 a.m. flight the day after diving works. ✅

One thing to keep in mind: if your plan includes a **night dive**, the 18 hours count from that night dive, so a 7:00 a.m. flight the next morning would not fit. In that case, the last dive would need to be the day before your flight day.

So, would you leave *from Cartagena* (Muelle de la Bodeguita)? 🚤

msg: Buenas tardes, somos una familia de Ciudad de México con tres hijos de 7, 11 y 14 años. Mi esposo y yo no tenemos certificación. ¿Qué actividades podemos hacer todos en las islas?

¡Qué buen plan familiar! En las Islas del Rosario pueden combinar actividades según la edad y experiencia de cada quien:

- **Tu hijo de 7 años:** puede hacer snorkel, que está disponible desde los 6 años.
- **Tu hijo de 11 años:** puede hacer el minicurso de buceo, sin certificación previa, o snorkel.
- **Tu hijo de 14 años:** puede hacer el minicurso o snorkel. El curso Avanzado requiere certificación previa.
- **Tú y tu esposo:** pueden hacer el minicurso de buceo sin certificación previa, o snorkel.

También es posible combinar buceo y snorkel en el mismo tour. Los menores deben ir acompañados por un padre o pariente responsable. ¿Ya estarán alojados en las islas o saldrían desde Cartagena?

reply:
¡Qué buen plan familiar! Como salen desde Cartagena, el punto de encuentro es el Muelle de la Bodeguita a las 8:00 a. m.; no hay recogida en el hotel y el transporte terrestre hasta el muelle no está incluido.

Para el minicurso, incluye entrenamiento en piscina, una inmersión en el mar con instructor PADI, equipo, lancha de ida y vuelta, almuerzo, seguro, entrada al Parque Nacional y aporte eco-social a DIVE TO HEAL. Es para mayores de 10 años, así que el niño de 7 puede hacer snorkel; los de 11 y 14 pueden elegir minicurso o snorkel. El snorkel incluye equipo, dos salidas guiadas, lancha, almuerzo, seguro, entrada al Parque y aporte eco-social. Te dejo los precios a continuación.

*Precios por persona* (online · normal):
• Minicurso de Buceo: 183 USD · 204 USD
• Tour de Snorkeling: 126 USD · 140 USD

*Descuento de grupo (5 personas o más):* 10% más, que se suma al 10% online (20% en total reservando online). No es automático: hay que pedirlo al equipo antes de pagar, o se pierde. No aplica a cursos PADI.

¿Te animas con el *minicurso*, el *snorkel* o el *curso Open Water*? 🌊

msg: Hello, my partner and I are staying at Hotel Cocoliso on Isla Grande this week. I'm a certified diver, she doesn't dive. Can we join something from the island?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Yes! Since you’re staying at Hotel Cocoliso, pick-up is included. You can join a one-dive trip for certified divers, and your partner can come along as a non-diving companion. The companion plan includes boat transport, insurance, and the National Natural Park entrance fee; lunch isn’t included.

You’ll need to show your certification card; if it’s been more than two years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• Fun Dives - 1 dive (1 day): 97 USD · 108 USD (345.000 COP · 383.000 COP)

Would you like to book these options?

msg: Do you pick us up at the hotel? What time, and do we need to bring our own gear?
reply:
Yes — since you're staying at Cocoliso, pick-up is confirmed and included, and the boat drops you back at the hotel afterwards. 🌊

Pick-up is between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (8:00 a.m. for specialties), and daytime activities end around 12:00–1:00 p.m. Times are fixed, so they can't be moved earlier or later.

No need to bring your own gear — diving and snorkeling gear is included in the dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and the PADI courses. Just bring swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. If you do bring your complete gear (regulator, BCD, wetsuit, mask, fins), there's a 5% discount on recreational diving and PADI courses.

You'll also need:
• For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
• To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.
• The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). The link can be sent together with the booking link; if you have not completed it, it is sent again in the booking confirmation email. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.
• If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.

Shall we go for the *2-dive trip* for you and, for your companion, the *mini-course*, *snorkeling* or just coming along on the *boat*? 🌊

msg: Queremos hacer las 2 inmersiones en un día. ¿Cómo reservamos todos juntos y cuándo hay que pedir el descuento?
reply:
¡Qué buen plan! Las dos inmersiones se hacen en puntos distintos de las Islas del Rosario. Para reservar los seis juntos, elige la misma fecha y 6 personas en el enlace de la salida desde Cartagena:

Antes de pagar, pidan al equipo que aplique el descuento de grupo. Para grupos de 5 o más, es 10% y se suma al 10% online; no se aplica automáticamente y, si pagan antes de solicitarlo, no se devuelve después. Como la reserva es de nacionalidades mixtas, el pago completo se hace en USD.

Si sales desde las islas, antes necesito saber tu hotel. ¿Saldrías *desde Cartagena* o ya estás *en las Islas del Rosario*? 🌊

msg: Hi, I'm a German traveler in Cartagena and I've never dived. I'd like to get my Open Water certification. How long does the course take?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

The Open Water course takes **2 days** and certifies you to dive down to **18 m**. It’s a great way to start diving! 🌊

From Cartagena, day 1 starts at **8:00 a.m.** at Muelle de la Bodeguita and includes pool training and two dives. You’ll stay overnight on the islands (accommodation isn’t included). On day 2, you’ll complete another pool session and two final dives, then return to Cartagena at **3:00 p.m.**, arriving around **4:15 p.m.** Lunch is included on day 1; day 2 lunch isn’t included.

The course also has an online PADI eLearning theory phase. Would you like the course price and booking link?

msg: Do I need to stay overnight on the islands, and is the hotel included in the price?
reply:
Yes, you do need to stay overnight on the islands — for the Open Water course there's no option to commute from Cartagena on both days. You stay at least one night, the night of day 1, since day 2 starts directly on the islands. 🌴

The hotel is **not included** in the course price — you book it directly with the hotel. Our dive base is at two hotels on Isla Grande: **Hotel San Pedro de Majagua** and **Hotel Cocoliso**, where pick-up is direct. You can also stay at other hotels in the area with maritime access, like Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras or Pao Pao.

How many people would this be for: just you, or more? 😊

msg: Actually, I only have two free days and I'm not sure I want a full course. What about just trying diving once without certification?
reply:
No worries at all — that's a great option! 🌊 The **Dive Mini Course** is exactly that: a one-day introductory dive, no certification needed and no prior experience required. You do the theory there on the day (nothing online or by email), pool practice, and one open water dive with an instructor. It's the perfect way to try it out and see how you feel.

Since you're departing from Cartagena, it's a same-day round trip: boat Cartagena–Islands–Cartagena included, lunch included, and all gear included.

One thing to keep in mind: the dive ends around 12:00 noon, and if you're flying afterwards you need to wait at least 12 hours from the last dive before your flight.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives): 316 USD · 351 USD
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

How many people would this be for: just you, or more? 😊

msg: ¿Ella puede hacer algo en el agua? ¿Y necesitaría algún permiso médico?
reply:
Sí, puede hacer snorkel en superficie, con el visto bueno de su médico. Durante el embarazo no se recomienda bucear con botella.

También necesitas:
• Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.
• Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh; los buzos muy experimentados (500+ inmersiones, Dive Master) los revisa un asesor del equipo. Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh y puedes bucear directamente. El refresher es el minicurso (piscina y una inmersión con instructor) y ocupa su propio día: ese mismo día no se hace la salida de buceo. Quien viene varios días hace el refresher el primero y bucea los demás.

No tenemos indicado un permiso médico específico para hacer snorkel; sí debe contar con la aprobación de su médico. 🌊

¿Te animas con la *salida de 2 inmersiones*, un *paquete de varios días* o un *curso avanzado*? 🌊

• 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives): 316 USD · 351 USD
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

Guests who are not Colombian or residents of Colombia pay in US dollars (USD) by card on the website; the rate is the same, only the currency changes.

msg: Hi, we're a group of 5 Canadian friends, all certified, staying in Cartagena. One of us is deaf. Can he dive with us?
reply:
Yes, absolutely — diving is for everyone, and the reef here is a wonderful place to share it. 🌊

Through our DIVE TO HEAL program we offer adaptive diving, and all our instructors are trained in adaptive diving. We've assisted more than 360 people with disabilities. Deaf divers can absolutely dive, and the logistics are coordinated case by case with the team to make sure everything runs smoothly.

Since you're all certified and staying in Cartagena, the natural fit would be our Fun Dives – 2 dives (1 day): same-day round trip from Cartagena, boat and lunch included, gear included.

A couple of things worth knowing:
- The only limitation for adaptive diving is the presence of additional medical conditions that contraindicate diving — the team reviews each case.
- The medical form is required, and the team coordinates the adaptive logistics in advance.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
*From Cartagena* — boat from Muelle de la Bodeguita · lunch included
• Fun Dives - 2 dives (1 day): 178 USD · 197 USD (630.000 COP · 700.000 COP)
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD (655.000 COP · 727.000 COP)
*Already on the Rosario Islands* — pickup at your hotel if it has boat access · no lunch
• Fun Dives - 2 dives (1 day): 124 USD · 138 USD (440.000 COP · 489.000 COP)
• Dive Mini Course: 134 USD · 149 USD (475.000 COP · 528.000 COP)

Would you leave *from Cartagena* or are you already *on the Rosario Islands*? Then I'll give you the exact plan. 🌊

msg: Un detalle: mi esposo buceó por última vez en abril de 2022 y yo en enero de este año, en Capurganá. ¿Eso cambia algo para él?
reply:
Sí, para él cambia: como su última inmersión fue en abril de 2022, normalmente necesitaría hacer un *refresher* antes de volver a bucear. El refresher ocupa un día completo y ese mismo día no se hace la salida de buceo; como van varios días, puede hacerlo el primer día y bucear los demás. Si ya hizo un refresher o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta y puede bucear directamente.

También necesitas:
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh; los buzos muy experimentados (500+ inmersiones, Dive Master) los revisa un asesor del equipo. Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh y puedes bucear directamente. El refresher es el minicurso (piscina y una inmersión con instructor) y ocupa su propio día: ese mismo día no se hace la salida de buceo. Quien viene varios días hace el refresher el primero y bucea los demás.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 18 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.
• Ser buzo certificado y presentar tu carnet

El *refresher* es un repaso con instructor antes de volver a bucear: se reserva como *Minicurso de Buceo* y cuesta *655.000 COP* por persona que lo necesite. Lleva el formulario médico de curso (aunque estén certificados, el enlace llega con la reserva). ¿Les interesa?

msg: Great, thanks. So the plan would be: my husband diving, our 11-year-old trying scuba for the first time, and me and our 6-year-old snorkeling, all on December 3 from Hotel Cocoliso. We're US citizens. How do we book and pay?
reply:
That sounds like a lovely family plan! Your husband can join certified fun dives, your 11-year-old can try the Dive Mini Course, and you and your 6-year-old can snorkel. Snorkeling is available from age 6, and the mini-course from age 10. Since you’re staying at Hotel Cocoliso, pickup is included. Lunch isn’t included for activities departing from the islands.

For your husband’s certified diving, the team books it in this chat. The mini-course and snorkeling are booked online, with the 10% online discount applied automatically:

- **Dive Mini Course:** https://book.divingplanet.org/book/dive-mini-course-already-on-island/20?language=en
- **Snorkeling:** https://book.divingplanet.org/book/snorkeling-already-on-the-island/25?language=en

As international guests, you pay in USD by card on the website. Payment is recorded right away, then the team reconciles it shortly after to confirm the booking. If the online payment fails, the team can provide a bank-transfer link. The booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before, so December 3 bookings need to be made before then.

There is always availability: we operate every day, including public holidays, except December 25 and January 1; if sea conditions are not safe, the trip is rescheduled.

For the one who hasn't chosen yet I'd recommend these options. Which one do they like best? 🐠
• *Certified diving* — Guided dives for already-certified divers; explore the reef at depth.
• *Dive mini-course* — A first time underwater with an instructor: pool training and a real dive. No experience needed.
• *Open Water course* — Entry certification course: qualifies you to dive independently down to 18 m.
• *Snorkeling* — Enjoy the reef from the surface, with mask and fins. Great for families.
• *Come along as a companion* — Comes on the boat and enjoys the day with the group, without getting in the water.

msg: Hello! My partner and I are from Dublin and we're staying in an Airbnb on Isla Grande from November 15 to 19. Could you pick us up there for a morning in the water?

Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Great that you'll be staying on Isla Grande — the Rosario Islands are a beautiful spot for a morning in the water. 🌊

Yes, if you're already on the islands and your accommodation has maritime access, boat pick-up and drop-off are included at no extra charge. In some cases the boat comes directly to the hotel/dock; in others we'll point you to the nearest dock or meeting point. The exact pick-up point and time are coordinated by a team advisor, who'll ask for the name of your Airbnb.

A couple of things to keep in mind:
- Pick-up from the islands is between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (8:00 a.m. for specialties), and daytime activities end around 12:00–1:00 p.m.
- If your Airbnb doesn't have maritime access, we'd arrange the nearest dock or meeting point.

To point you to the right plan, could you tell me a bit more about what you'd like to do — a fun dive (are you both certified?), a mini course, or snorkeling? And do you know if your Airbnb has boat access?

msg: I'm a PADI Open Water diver, my last dive was in Thailand in May 2025. My partner has never dived and would like to try the mini course. We'd like to go on Tuesday, November 17.
reply:
Perfect! 🙌

msg: A health question: my partner had asthma as a child and used an inhaler, but hasn't needed it in more than ten years. Is that a problem for the mini course? Is there a form to fill in?
reply:
For the asthma question, a team member needs to review your partner’s specific case, so I can’t advise whether it’s a problem for the mini-course. The medical form is required for mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (it’s in Spanish).

You'll also need:
• Be ready at 9:30 a.m. at your hotel
• To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.
• After diving, wait at least 12 hours before flying
• Minimum age: 10 and over.
• What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.

For specific medical questions, it's important that you speak with our qualified staff so they can assess your particular situation. I'm passing you now to someone from our team, who will write to you here shortly.

msg: ¿Los niños pueden bucear con esas edades? Al de 9 le encanta el mar, pero no sé si es muy chico para el minicurso.
reply:
¡Sí, los dos pueden disfrutar del mar! Con 9 años, el minicurso todavía no está disponible: es desde los 10. Pero puede hacer snorkel desde los 6 o *Bubble Makers*, para niños de 8 a 10 años, en piscina o aguas muy poco profundas (máximo 2 m) y con un instructor dedicado. Si quieres, te ayudo a reservar: *Minicurso de buceo*. ¿Te animas? 🌊

msg: Gracias. Entonces sería el domingo 13 de diciembre desde Cartagena: mi esposo a bucear, el de 13 y yo al minicurso, y para el de 9 lo que le corresponda por su edad. ¿Cómo hacemos la reserva y cuánto hay que pagar por adelantado?
reply:
Para el domingo 13 de diciembre, desde Cartagena, pueden reservar en línea eligiendo la fecha y las personas. El minicurso cuesta **183 USD por persona** con el 10% de descuento online; el buceo certificado de 2 inmersiones cuesta **178 USD por persona** online. Para el niño de 9 años, las opciones son *snorkel* o *Bubble Makers* (buceo introductorio para niños de 8 a 10 años, en piscina o aguas muy poco profundas, máximo 2 m, con instructor dedicado). El de 13 puede hacer el minicurso; para bucear como certificado necesita tener certificación Open Water. Los menores deben ir acompañados de un adulto responsable.

Como pagan en dólares, se requiere el **100% al reservar**, con tarjeta extranjera y usando el pasaporte como documento de identificación. El descuento online se aplica al reservar por la web. Aquí tienes los enlaces:

- [Minicurso de buceo](https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=es)
- [Buceo certificado, 2 inmersiones](https://book.divingplanet.org/book/salidas-de-buceo/1?language=es)

Siempre hay disponibilidad: operamos todos los días, festivos incluidos, salvo el 25 de diciembre y el 1 de enero; si el mar no está apto, la salida se reprograma.

🤿

Para una primera vez te recomiendo el *minicurso*: teoría, práctica en aguas tranquilas y una inmersión en el mar con instructor, sin necesidad de experiencia. Si lo que buscas es certificarte, está el *curso PADI Open Water*. ¿Te animas con el minicurso? 🤿

msg: Hola, ¿qué tal? Somos una pareja de Córdoba, Argentina, y queremos sacar la certificación de buceo en Cartagena. Vamos a estar allá del 1 al 8 de diciembre.
reply:

msg: ¿Cómo es el curso Open Water con ustedes? ¿Cuántos días dura, hay que estudiar algo antes y se puede ir y volver a Cartagena cada día?
reply:
¡Es una experiencia buenísima para empezar a bucear! El Open Water dura **2 días** y combina teoría, práctica en piscina y **4 inmersiones en aguas abiertas**.

Antes de comenzar la parte práctica, debes completar la teoría en **PADI eLearning**, que toma aproximadamente **10 a 12 horas**. El curso requiere alojarse al menos una noche en las Islas del Rosario: el primer día no se regresa a Cartagena, así que no se puede ir y volver desde Cartagena ambos días. El alojamiento no está incluido y se reserva directamente con el hotel.

Saliendo desde Cartagena, el primer día la lancha sale del Muelle de la Bodeguita a las 8:00 a. m. y haces piscina y dos inmersiones; después vas al hotel en las islas. El segundo día haces la sesión final de piscina y las dos inmersiones restantes, y regresas a Cartagena en la lancha de las 3:00 p. m. (llegada aproximada a las 4:15 p. m.). El almuerzo está incluido el primer día, no el segundo.

También necesitas:
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

¿Saldrías *desde Cartagena* o ya estás *en las Islas del Rosario*? Así te paso el plan exacto. 🌊

El precio del Curso Open Water incluye la tarifa de ingreso al Parque Nacional Natural, seguro de buceo obligatorio, lancha rápida Cartagena–Islas–Cartagena, entrenamiento en piscina, 4 inmersiones de certificación con instructor PADI, equipo de buceo para la práctica, almuerzo el primer día, tarjeta de certificación PADI y aporte eco-social a DIVE TO HEAL.

Políticas de Diving Planet:
- Esperar al menos 18 horas para tomar un avión después de buceo recreativo. 12 horas mínimo después del minicurso (solo para quien no está certificado). El refresher también son 18 horas: es para buzos certificados, aunque se reserve como el minicurso. Las horas se cuentan desde la última inmersión, no desde la vuelta a Cartagena. La inmersión del minicurso termina hacia las 12:00 (mediodía): sus 12 horas se cuentan desde ahí. Si la última inmersión es de día, también la del refresher (las actividades acaban hacia las 12:00-13:00), se puede volar desde las 7:00 a. m. del día siguiente; tras el minicurso, desde la medianoche de ese mismo día. Si la última es nocturna, las horas se cuentan desde ella. Un vuelo al día siguiente a las 7:00 a. m. o más tarde SÍ llega: se puede bucear el día anterior, y la hora de vuelta a Cartagena de ese día no cambia nada. Para un buzo certificado, un vuelo el MISMO día de la inmersión NUNCA llega, sea a la hora que sea, también por la noche: con un vuelo el domingo por la noche, la última inmersión tiene que ser como muy tarde el sábado; que la lancha vuelva antes de irse no lo arregla. Quien dice que se va ese día sin decir cómo, probablemente vuela: dile esto. Al contestar, di primero desde qué hora puede volar y después compáralo con su vuelo; no empieces por sí o no.
- Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh; los buzos muy experimentados (500+ inmersiones, Dive Master) los revisa un asesor del equipo. Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh y puedes bucear directamente. El refresher es el minicurso (piscina y una inmersión con instructor) y ocupa su propio día: ese mismo día no se hace la salida de buceo. Quien viene varios días hace el refresher el primero y bucea los demás.
- Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.
- Muelle de la Bodeguita, a 5 minutos del centro histórico, a las 8:00 AM. Saliendo desde Cartagena no hay recogida en el hotel: cada persona llega por su cuenta al muelle (el transporte terrestre hasta el muelle no está incluido).
- Al reservar aceptas nuestros términos y condiciones, política de cancelación y tratamiento de datos personales. Ver: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Los cambios de fecha están sujetos a disponibilidad y a nuestros términos y condiciones. Ver: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Los cambios en el número de personas de una reserva ya hecha están sujetos a disponibilidad y a nuestros términos y condiciones. Ver: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Pagan en pesos colombianos (COP) los colombianos (quien tiene la nacionalidad colombiana, con cédula o pasaporte colombiano, viva donde viva; también con doble nacionalidad, si una es la colombiana) y los residentes en Colombia (quien tiene cédula de extranjería, que es un documento de residente; vivir en Colombia sin ella no basta). Decir que es colombiano o de una ciudad de Colombia ("soy de Cali") ya lo dice; lo que no basta es solo haber nacido allí viviendo fuera: entonces se le pregunta si tiene la nacionalidad colombiana o cédula de extranjería. El resto de clientes internacionales paga en dólares (USD). Un grupo no se paga por partes: si en la misma reserva hay colombianos o residentes y también extranjeros sin cédula de extranjería, todo el grupo paga en dólares (USD), también los residentes y los colombianos. Un colombiano con quien tiene cédula de extranjería, sea de donde sea, no es un grupo mixto: pagan los dos en pesos (COP). El precio es el mismo: solo cambia la moneda (no hay descuento por ser colombiano).
- Si en el grupo hay colombianos o residentes y también extranjeros sin cédula de extranjería, toda la reserva del grupo se paga en dólares (USD), al mismo precio equivalente. Quien tiene cédula de extranjería no cuenta como extranjero, sea de donde sea. No hay un precio distinto por ser colombiano.
- Si ya estás en las Islas del Rosario, coordinamos recogida y regreso desde hoteles con acceso marítimo. En algunos casos la lancha llega directo al hotel; en otros te indicamos el muelle o punto más cercano.
- Estos planes manejan precios diferentes porque no incluyen transporte desde Cartagena ni almuerzo.
- La recogida es solo en las Islas del Rosario: Barú (también Playa Blanca, que está en Barú) no es parte de las islas y allí no operamos ni recogemos; quien se aloja en Barú sale desde Cartagena (Muelle de la Bodeguita).
- Depende de la actividad: snorkeling desde los 6 años; Bubble Makers de 8 a 10 años (minicurso en piscina y aguas poco profundas, máx. 2 metros); minicurso de buceo y curso Open Water desde los 10 años; Curso Avanzado (Advanced) y curso Rescue desde los 12. Menores de edad deben estar acompañados por un padre o pariente responsable demostrable.

- No se permite llevar ni tomar alcohol en la lancha ni durante la actividad, y no se puede consumir alcohol u otras sustancias antes de bucear. Debes presentarte en buen estado físico.
- El sistema de reservas de la página web. Se cierra automáticamente a las 4:30 PM del día anterior: pasada esa hora ya no se puede reservar para el día siguiente, y se reserva igual por la web para el siguiente día disponible.
- Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
- Desde Cartagena: salida a las 8:00 a.m. desde el Muelle de la Bodeguita y regreso a las 3:00 p.m. (llegada aprox. 4:15 p.m.). Desde las islas: recogida en el hotel entre las 9:30 y las 9:45 (a las 8:00 en las especialidades y a las 7:30 el día 2 de algunos cursos). Las actividades de día terminan hacia las 12:00-13:00 (ver el horario de las actividades). Buceo nocturno: por la tarde-noche (recogida hacia las 5:30 p.m. y regreso hacia las 7:30 p.m.). Sistema de reservas online cierra a las 4:30 p.m. del día anterior; pasada esa hora se reserva por la web para el siguiente día disponible.
- Solo cerramos el 25 de diciembre y el 1 de enero. El resto del año operamos todos los días, incluyendo festivos, salvo suspensión por condiciones meteorológicas adversas.
- El tour incluye agua todo el día, dulces de coco entre inmersiones y almuerzo (arroz con pollo o arroz con vegetales). El menú es siempre el mismo, no cambia según día/proveedor. Vegetarianos, veganos y celíacos reciben arroz con vegetales. El cliente puede llevar su propia comida si lo necesita (ej. alergia o dieta especial). Si el cliente tiene alguna alergia alimentaria, debe informarnos antes del tour. En los paquetes de varios días saliendo desde Cartagena el almuerzo va incluido solo el primer día; en los planes de quien ya está en las islas no se incluye almuerzo.

Vale para todas las actividades, también el minicurso (y el refresher, que se reserva como minicurso), los cursos PADI y las salidas de buzos certificados: no incluidas, el instructor puede hacerlas voluntariamente.

Lo mismo en los paquetes de buceo de varios días (4, 5, 7 y 9 inmersiones): se duerme en las islas y el alojamiento, que no está incluido, se reserva directamente con el hotel.

Se aceptan: discapacidad auditiva (sordos), discapacidad visual (ciegos), movilidad reducida (silla de ruedas), Síndrome de Down, Parálisis Cerebral y Autismo (según nivel y evaluación). Todos los instructores están formados en buceo adaptado. Se recomienda avisar con anticipación. La limitación es la presencia de condiciones médicas adicionales que contraindiquen el buceo.
- Si ya estás en las Islas del Rosario y tu hotel tiene acceso marítimo, la recogida y el regreso en lancha están incluidos sin cargo adicional.
- Buceamos en las Islas del Rosario, dentro del Parque Nacional Natural Corales del Rosario y San Bernardo, a unos 45-60 minutos en lancha desde Cartagena.
- Todas las actividades de día (salidas de buceo, minicurso, snorkel, cursos y cada día de los paquetes) terminan hacia las 12:00-13:00, y después viene la comida. Quien sale desde Cartagena tiene el almuerzo incluido en las islas y la lancha regresa a Cartagena a las 3:00 p.m. (llegada aprox. 4:15 p.m.); quien está alojado en las islas vuelve a su hotel hacia las 12:00-13:00 a comer (almuerzo no incluido). - Las actividades y los cursos se dan en español y en inglés. Si un participante no habla ninguno de los dos idiomas, puede venir con alguien que le haga de intérprete, pero la instrucción sigue siendo en español o en inglés.
- Se reserva por la página web, en el enlace de cada actividad (con el 10% de descuento online). Es igual saliendo desde Cartagena o ya en las islas: no hay teoría online ni por correo; la teoría se hace allí, el mismo día, junto con la práctica en piscina y 1 inmersión en el mar con instructor.
- Los clientes extranjeros pagan el 100 % con tarjeta en la página web; con una tarjeta extranjera se usa el pasaporte como documento de identificación.
- Los colombianos y los residentes en Colombia (también quien tiene cédula de extranjería) pagan en pesos y no usan el enlace de reserva de la web: la reserva siempre la cierra un asesor del equipo por este chat, que les envía el enlace, el QR o Llave para pagar el 100 % online o un anticipo del 50 %, y el otro 50 % el día de la actividad, con tarjeta o efectivo. El anticipo del 50 % es solo para ellos. Nadie paga el 100 % en el muelle sin haber reservado online.

msg: Sounds good. Five of us, all US citizens, staying at San Pedro de Majagua: four divers on January 15 and 16 and one snorkeler on those same days. What's the next step to book and pay?
reply:
For the four certified divers, the 2-day, 4-dive package is **USD 204 per person online** from the islands. It includes four daytime dives and gear; lunch isn’t included. There’s no online booking link for this package, so a team advisor needs to arrange it. Would you like me to connect you with one?

For the snorkeler, book the Snorkeling Tour separately here: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/snorkeling-already-on-the-island/25?language=en. The online price is **USD 45 per person**, and the 10% online discount is applied automatically. International clients pay 100% by card on the website; with a foreign card, use the passport as the ID document. Payment is recorded right away, then the team reconciles it shortly after to confirm the booking. If online payment fails, the team can send a bank-transfer link and the online discount is kept.

Guests who are not Colombian or residents of Colombia pay in US dollars (USD) by card on the website; the rate is the same, only the currency changes.

msg: ¿Tenemos que dormir en las islas? ¿Qué incluye y qué no incluye cada plan, por ejemplo el hotel y las comidas?
reply:
Sí: para tu Curso Referido de 2 días deben dormir al menos una noche en las islas; el día 1 no se regresa a Cartagena. El alojamiento no está incluido y se reserva directamente con el hotel.

Saliendo desde Cartagena, tu curso incluye la lancha ida y vuelta, equipo, seguro, entrada al Parque Nacional y almuerzo el primer día. No incluye hotel, transporte terrestre hasta el muelle, fotos o videos submarinos, propinas ni comida adicional al almuerzo.

Para tu novio, las opciones son buceo certificado, snorkel o ir de acompañante en la lancha. El plan de acompañante incluye lancha, almuerzo, seguro y entrada al Parque; no incluye alojamiento ni equipo de buceo o snorkel. Si bucea, el plan incluye equipo y almuerzo según el plan elegido. El regreso a Cartagena en una fecha distinta a la del plan no está incluido.

Para recomendar lo que mejor le encaje a quien aún no ha elegido: ¿van a estar *un solo día* o *varios días*? 🌊
